title: SYSK Selects: Was there a real King Arthur?
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the January 14, 2014 episode "Was there a real King Arthur?" Josh and Chuck trace the Arthurian legend from its Celtic oral roots through early Welsh poetry (Y Gododdin), Historia Regum Britannie by Geoffrey of Monmouth, the Vulgate Cycle and Grail stories, Thomas Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur, Tennyson and T. H. White, then examine which people and places (Merlin, Camelot candidates like Tintagel and Cadbury Castle, Glastonbury/Avalon and the reputed grave of Arthur and Guinevere, Bedivere, Kay, and Roman-era candidates) might have a basis in real history. A listener mail segment about a listener's late father closes the episode.

segments.title: Selects intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Chuck introduces the pick, Was there a Real King Arthur? from January 2014. The hosts banter about the 1980s film Excalibur, the 1975 Monty Python and the Holy Grail, and Camelot the musical.
topics: Monty Python and the Holy Grail

segments.title: Basic Arthurian legend and Celtic roots
segments.summary: The hosts summarize the Arthur story: a king who restored peace to Britain after Roman withdrawal and Saxon incursions, built Camelot, and founded the Round Table. They explain the legend is syncretic, with Christian elements layered on Celtic oral myths, and note Pliny the Elder as an outside source on the Celts.

segments.title: Sword in the stone, Excalibur and Lady of the Lake
segments.summary: They recount the varying versions of how Arthur got the sword: pulling it from a stone, from the Lady of the Lake, or from a sword breaking and being replaced by Excalibur. They discuss Merlin, Avalon, and digress into apple folklore.

segments.title: Arthur's reign, Guinevere, Mordred and death at Camlan
segments.summary: They cover Arthur's marriage to Guinevere, the knights of the Round Table, the betrayal by Mordred and Morgan le Fay, the battle at Camlan, and Arthur's sword being returned to the lake. They note Arthur's return as the Once and Future King.

segments.title: Literary history: Y Gododdin, Geoffrey of Monmouth, Vulgate Cycle
segments.summary: The hosts trace the written record: the early Welsh poem Y Gododdin mentioning Arthur, the Historia Brittonum and Annales Cambriae, Geoffrey of Monmouth's Historia Regum Britanniae, and French romances like the Vulgate Cycle that added Lancelot, the Grail quest and Christian elements.

segments.title: Malory, Tennyson, T. H. White and later adaptations
segments.summary: They discuss Thomas Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur as the major compilation that shifted focus to Christianity, along with additions like the Lady of the Lake and Mordred as Arthur's son, and later works by Tennyson and T. H. White, including The Sword in the Stone.

segments.title: Was Merlin real? Druid candidates
segments.summary: The hosts consider whether Merlin existed, suggesting he may derive from two late sixth-century holy men, Myrddin Wyllt and Emrys, one a wild man after war and the other a druid prophet.

segments.title: Candidate Camelot sites: Tintagel, Cadbury, Winchester
segments.summary: They evaluate places claimed as Camelot. Tintagel Castle has an inscription naming a descendant of Arthur, though the castle as built dates to the 1100s and the site was settled earlier. Winchester's wooden round table was carbon dated to Henry VIII's era. Cadbury Castle in Somerset is considered the most plausible Camelot candidate.

segments.title: Glastonbury and Avalon, Arthur's reputed grave
segments.summary: They discuss Glastonbury as Avalon, the twelfth-century monks' claimed discovery of Arthur and Guinevere's grave with an inscribed cross, the later finding that the inscription was in twelfth-century Latin, and excavations finding sixth-century graves. They conclude the identity remains unproven.

segments.title: Real candidates for Arthur and his knights
segments.summary: They cover possible real-life knights Bedivere and Kay, who appear in Welsh texts such as the Mabinogion, and candidates for Arthur himself: Roman commander Lucius Artorius Castus, Aurelius Ambrosius, a Welsh king Arthwys, and the idea that Arthur may be a title meaning bear.

segments.title: Travel tangent and Monty Python wrap-up
segments.summary: The hosts chat about visiting Rome and the Colosseum, then tie the legend's persistence to romance and chivalry and mention Monty Python's Black Knight scene.

segments.title: Listener mail: tribute to a father
segments.summary: Megan from Plano, Texas writes that her late father Howard, a tinkerer who encouraged her to read about random topics, would have enjoyed the show. Josh and Chuck respond warmly.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact info
segments.summary: Josh invites listeners to search for King Arthur on the site and to get in touch via Twitter, Facebook, email, or the website.
